newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Highland seeks price rises abroad.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Highland seeks price rises abroad.

text.p: Scotch whisky maker Highland Distilleries Co Plc expects to achieve an overall 1997 price increase of about two percent on its brands overseas, chief executive Brian Ivory said on Tuesday.
"About two percent on average in 1997 will be achievable overseas," said Ivory in an interview.
In Britain, Highland announced a price rise of just over four percent, which comes into effect in mid-April, on its leading brand Famous Grouse.
"Our assessment of the market is that we feel it will stick," said Ivory.
Overseas sales of the Famous Grouse grew five percent on a like-for-like basis in the six months ended February 28, 1997.
The main increases were in Greece, the Netherlands and Sweden while France was disappointing. Exports to North America and Asia showed strong growth.
But in Britain the market remains very competitive with industry sales down by five percent in the period.
"I think European economies will continue to find the going tough in trying to fit into the Maastricht corset in the run up to a single currency," said Ivory.
"But I think we will see growth in continental Europe albeit against the background of a difficult market."

The company's single malt whisky Macallan suffered from heavy price competition over the critical Christmas period. Highland refused to take part in the heavy promotional activity and price discounting offered by its competitors.
In North America, exports of Famous Grouse rose 19 percent in the period and sales of single malt Macallan were up 20 percent, the strongest increase in sales to the region for a decade, said Ivory.
"I think the market for spirits in North America probably has turned a corner, but how sharp the corner and how steep the trend I am not sure."
"Certainly the demand for Scotch and the image of Scotch has improved, it is now considered a prestigious product again."
Earlier the company reported a 41 percent increase in pre-tax profits to 19.4 million stg in the six months ended February 28, 1997.
Highland shares were off 1-1/2p at 342-1/2p in early trade.
